articles.title: An 85-year-old Massachusetts man allegedly sent more than $1 million to a woman he was dating for taxes on farmland she said she would inherit in Brazil; prosecutors say the land and inheritance never existed
articles.summary: An 85-year-old man from Massachusetts who had health and memory problems sent more than $1 million to a woman he was dating.
articles.body: An 85-year-old man from Massachusetts who had health and memory problems sent more than $1 million to a woman he was dating. She allegedly told him she needed the money to pay taxes and legal fees on farmland she was expected to inherit in Brazil, federal prosecutors say. According to the US Attorney's Office for the District of Massachusetts, the farmland, inheritance tax and lawyers did not exist. Maria Auxiliadora Rezende, 66, of Revere, Massachusetts, has been indicted by a federal grand jury on one count of wire fraud. Federal agents arrested her and charged her through a criminal complaint on 10 November 2026. The grand jury indictment was announced on 13 November 2026.How prosecutors say the scheme workedCourt documents filed in federal court in Boston say Rezende began a romantic relationship with the 85-year-old man. Authorities have not released his name or hometown. Prosecutors say Rezende falsely told the man that she was going to inherit farmland in Brazil. She allegedly convinced him that he could earn money from the property if he helped pay a supposed Brazilian inheritance tax and related legal costs. Federal investigators say the entire story was made up. According to the U.S. Attorney's Office, the farmland did not exist. Neither did the Brazilian inheritance tax, the lawyers or the legal fees. During the alleged fraud, the man transferred more than $1 million to Rezende and her associates, according to the court documents. The filings mention other people who allegedly helped receive the money. However, prosecutors have not announced charges against anyone else.How the allegations came to lightAccording to reporting by Brazilian Times, a Massachusetts newspaper that covers the Brazilian community, the victim is a retired professor who had been in a relationship with Rezende since 2013. Brazilian Times reported that the man's relatives became worried after noticing repeated money transfers. They began asking questions about why he was sending so much money and why the requests kept coming. The family then hired a lawyer in Brazil to check whether the farmland actually existed. They also asked the lawyer to examine the documents and claims that had been shown to their relative. According to Brazilian Times, the private investigation found problems with the inheritance story. This led to further checks by US federal authorities. The newspaper also reported that federal agents arrested Rezende on 10 November 2026, as she was preparing to travel to Brazil.Federal agencies and potential penaltiesThe case was announced by United States Attorney Leah B. Foley and Thomas Demeo, Special Agent in Charge of the Boston Field Office of the Internal Revenue Service's Criminal Investigation division. Homeland Security Investigations in New England and the U.S. Secret Service's Boston Field Office also helped investigate the case, according to the Department of Justice. Assistant US Attorney Kristen Kearney, who works in the Securities, Financial and Cyber Fraud Unit, is handling the prosecution. Under federal law, wire fraud carries a maximum sentence of 20 years in prison. A conviction can also lead to up to three years of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000. However, these are the maximum possible penalties. The final sentence would be decided by a federal district court judge. The judge would consider the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other legal factors before deciding the punishment.A pattern of romance fraud against older adults?Federal consumer protection figures show that romance scams and investment fraud continue to cause major financial losses for older Americans. In its annual report to Congress, Protecting Older Consumers 2025-2026, the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) reported that older adults reported losing around $3 billion to fraud in 2025. This was a sharp increase from approximately $600 million in 2020. The FTC said much of this increase came from individual cases involving losses of more than $100,000. These cases often involved investment scams, romance scams and schemes in which criminals pretended to be trusted people or organizations. The FTC also found that older adults reported much higher median financial losses than younger people. They were also more likely to report losing money to romance scams.Many victims do not report fraud because they feel embarrassed or afraid to tell others what happened. For this reason, the FTC estimated that the actual cost of fraud against older adults in 2025 could have been between $13.3 billion and $119.5 billion, depending on the method used to calculate the losses. Figures from law enforcement agencies in New England show a similar problem. In a public warning issued in February 2026, the FBI's Boston division reported that more than 700 people across Massachusetts, Maine, New Hampshire and Rhode Island said they had lost around $20 million to romance scams during 2025.The figures were included in an FBI Boston warning published on 9 February 2026. articles.title: Man dies after being hit by ambulance on A19 near Sunderland
articles.summary: Northumbria Police says a man in his 30s died at the scene on the A19 near Sunderland.
articles.body:
A man has died after being struck by an ambulance transporting a patient near Sunderland, police have said.

Northumbria Police said the crash occurred on the A19, between the junctions for the A1018 and A690, shortly after 02:00 GMT.

The ambulance was travelling on the northbound carriageway and did not have its blue lights on when it hit the man, who was in his 30s and died at the scene.

Neither the patient nor their partner who were travelling in the ambulance were injured in the collision, while the vehicle's driver, a man in his 40s, was also not hurt and remained at the scene to assist police with their inquiries.

The North East Ambulance Service (NEAS) said the patient in the ambulance and their partner were transferred to another ambulance.

Officers from Northumbria Police's roads unit have launched an investigation into the collision.

Sgt Ben Rutherford said: "Our thoughts are firmly with the family and loved ones of the man who has tragically died following this collision.

"We will continue to support them in any way that we can at this incredibly difficult time."

Anyone with CCTV or dashcam footage of the incident itself or the moments leading up to the collision has been urged to contact the force.

Rutherford said anyone with information, no matter how insignificant it may seem, "could prove key to our investigation and help provide answers for the man's loved ones".

A NEAS spokesperson said: "Around [02:00] one of our ambulance crews was involved in a road traffic incident with a pedestrian on the A19 northbound, while transporting a patient and their partner to a nearby hospital.

"We dispatched a number of resources to the scene.

"The patient on board and their partner were transferred to another ambulance and taken to hospital for further treatment.

"Sadly, despite the best efforts of our crews attending, the patient injured as the result of the collision passed away at the scene.

"This is a hugely tragic incident for all involved.

"Our thoughts and condolences are with the patient's loved ones.

"We will now, of course, be working closely with the police to support their investigation."

articles.title: Psychology says people who always try to step on alternate floor tiles may be turning an ordinary walk into a pattern-following game
articles.summary: You are walking along a tiled floor when you notice that your feet are landing on alternate tiles.
articles.body: You are walking along a tiled floor when you notice that your feet are landing on alternate tiles. Instead of stepping wherever your next foot naturally falls, you begin following a pattern: one tile, skip the next, step on the third. Sometimes you avoid the lines between tiles or try to keep both feet within a particular sequence.You may not even realise when you start doing it. For some people, the habit continues until the floor pattern ends. For others, it is simply a small game they play while walking through a corridor, shopping centre or railway station.This seemingly insignificant behaviour may be connected to the human tendency to notice patterns, create order and turn repetitive movements into small challenges. It does not necessarily indicate anything unusual about a person's personality.Why does the brain enjoy finding patterns in ordinary things?Humans are naturally good at recognising patterns. We notice repetition, symmetry and order in objects around us, sometimes even when we are not deliberately looking for them. A 2012 study examined how people create and perceive visual patterns. In a series of experiments, participants were asked to arrange visual elements into patterns.The researchers found that people spontaneously created highly ordered arrangements and generally preferred ordered patterns over random ones. The study suggests that the mind readily organises visual information into familiar structures.This offers one possible explanation for why a tiled floor can become more than just a surface to walk on. Its repeated squares, lines and alternating colours provide an easy structure for the mind to follow. Skipping every alternate tile turns that visual arrangement into a simple movement-based pattern.However, the study examined how people organise and perceive visual patterns. It did not test whether people who step on alternate tiles have a stronger preference for patterns.Why can walking become a little game?A familiar route can sometimes become an opportunity to create a small challenge. A person may decide to step only on dark tiles, avoid the joints between slabs or follow a repeating sequence without interrupting their stride. The activity can make an otherwise routine walk feel more engaging. It gives the person a simple rule to follow and a small goal to complete.Research on how people respond to floor patterns also shows that visual arrangements can influence the experience of walking. In a 2021 study titled ‘Walking on Visual Illusions,’ researchers from the University of Bristol and other institutions observed participants walking across floors printed with different visual patterns.Participants found the patterns interesting, with some describing them as playful or gentle. Others found certain designs uncomfortable to walk on and reported feeling less stable. The study focused on how visual floor designs affect walking experience, rather than why people deliberately step on alternate tiles. Still, it shows that the patterns beneath our feet can influence how we experience an ordinary walk.When is it just a harmless habit?For many people, stepping on alternate tiles is simply a passing activity. They may do it without thinking, stop when the floor changes or forget about it a few minutes later. Similar repetitive routines are also seen during childhood. A 2002 study examined rituals, habits and magical beliefs in 31 children.The researchers found associations between children's ritualistic behaviours and their beliefs about magic and wishes. The study described these behaviours as part of the range of repetitive habits that can occur during typical development.But there is an important contrast between enjoying a pattern and feeling compelled to follow it. If someone deliberately avoids a particular tile because it makes walking more entertaining, the behaviour is unlikely to be concerning. If they feel intense anxiety when they break the sequence, believe something bad will happen if they step on the wrong tile, or find themselves unable to stop repeating the action, the experience is different.Repetitive movements alone do not establish obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). What matters is whether the behaviour causes significant distress, takes up considerable time or interferes with everyday activities.Does stepping on alternate tiles say something about your personality?Not necessarily. There is no established evidence that people who follow floor patterns are more creative, organised or detail-oriented than others. For some, it may be a playful way to pass the time. For others, it may simply be an automatic habit they picked up during childhood and continued into adulthood.The next time you find yourself skipping every alternate tile, it may just be your mind turning an ordinary walk into a small pattern-following game. The habit becomes more meaningful only when it stops being a choice and starts feeling like something you must do.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: British Columbia's Conservatives have won power for the first time since 1928, taking 64 of 93 seats and ending nine years of NDP rule; the party promises to expand natural gas output amid US tariff tensions
articles.summary: British Columbia has elected a Conservative majority government in a historic political shift, ending nine years of New Democratic Party (NDP) rule and
articles.body: British Columbia has elected a Conservative majority government in a historic political shift, ending nine years of New Democratic Party (NDP) rule and putting energy development at the centre of the incoming administration's economic agenda. According to Reuters, the October 24 provincial election delivered a decisive victory to the Conservatives, who campaigned on expanding liquefied natural gas (LNG) production and reducing regulatory barriers for businesses. Reporting by The Canadian Press and CityNews also highlighted the scale of the party's breakthrough and the challenges facing the defeated NDP. Scroll down to read more…A major shift in provincial politicsThe Conservatives secured 64 of the 93 seats in the provincial legislature, well above the 47 required for a majority. The NDP won 27 seats, while the Green Party secured two, according to preliminary results reported by CityNews and analysed by Open Data Canada. The result represents the Conservatives’ first provincial election victory since 1928.The scale of the defeat was particularly significant for the NDP, which won 47 seats in the 2024 election. Premier David Eby conceded defeat and announced that he would step down as party leader, leaving the NDP to regroup in opposition. The Conservatives' victory also came despite polls suggesting a considerably narrower contest. Open Data Canada's analysis of preliminary results found that the party secured approximately 48% of the popular vote, compared with around 37% for the NDP and 11% for the Greens. The Conservatives gained ground across the province, with 21 constituencies switching from the NDP to the Conservatives.Natural gas expansion takes centre stageEnergy policy is expected to be a defining feature of the new government's agenda. The Conservatives have pledged to double British Columbia's natural gas production by 2032 and more than triple it by 2035, alongside faster approvals for major projects and fewer regulatory hurdles for resource companies.The party's platform also includes changes to emissions limits and the province's carbon tax framework. It has signalled plans to reconnect with major energy companies that withdrew from British Columbia's liquefied natural gas sector after 2018, including ExxonMobil, Chevron and Woodside, according to Reuters.The proposed expansion could strengthen the province's position in the global LNG market and encourage further investment in energy infrastructure. However, delivering on these commitments will depend on project approvals, investment decisions, infrastructure development and market conditions.Tariff tensions add urgency to the economic agendaThe election took place against a backdrop of trade tensions with the United States under President Donald Trump. Tariff threats have added uncertainty for Canadian businesses and exporters, making economic resilience a central issue for provincial leaders. Eby had sought a renewed mandate to respond to the trade dispute, while the Conservatives campaigned on a different approach, emphasising resource development, business investment and regulatory reform.The outcome gives the incoming government a strong legislative majority to pursue its proposals. Cost-of-living pressures and healthcare were also among the issues occupying voters during the campaign. The new administration will therefore face expectations beyond energy policy, including delivering economic relief while addressing public-service needs.Fiscal challenges await the incoming governmentThe Conservatives will inherit a difficult fiscal position. An analysis published by TD Economics on October 26 noted that British Columbia's 2026 budget projected a deficit of C$13.3 billion for the 2026-27 fiscal year, with further shortfalls expected over the following two years.The party has proposed tax relief, spending restraint and a review of government operations to support its economic programme. Yet the success of that approach will depend partly on whether faster project development and stronger economic activity generate enough additional revenue to offset the cost of its commitments.For now, the election marks a turning point in British Columbia's political direction. With the Conservatives preparing to take office, their ability to translate promises on energy, taxation and economic growth into tangible results will shape the province's next chapter.You use AI every day. articles.title: Bahrain accuses Iran of attacking its territory to ‘settle’ score with US
articles.summary: Tehran says its air attacks on countries cooperating with the US are justified under international law.
articles.body:
Bahrain’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has denounced what it describes as “a resumption of Iran’s aggression” after the latest air attacks on its Riffa Air Base by Tehran.

In a statement, the ministry said the attacks on Sunday launched by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) violated international law and “no pretext can legitimise violations of state sovereignty”.

“Bahrain also rejects the use of its territory to settle accounts and holds Iran fully responsible for the attacks and their consequences,” the statement added.

Bahrain’s military said its defence systems intercepted several Iranian “aerial attacks” targeting the kingdom. Its Riffa Air Base is used by the United States military.

The IRGC has not commented. It had said on Friday that it launched an attack on a US early warning radar facility in Bahrain and destroyed it. Bahrain said it intercepted two drones that day.

Al Jazeera’s Resul Serdar, reporting from Tehran, noted that Iran had held back amid intermittent US attacks in the past weeks but in the past three days, it has fired twice at Bahrain.

“We were seeing the United States’s low-intensity warfare being conducted against Iran. From time to time, the US attacked Iran’s military assets – telecommunications towers specifically – in the southern part of the country,” he said.

But that appears to have changed. “It seems this is now the new rule of engagement,” Serdar added.

Iran’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei defended Tehran’s attacks and accused Gulf countries of aiding US strikes against Iran.

“All the cases that indicate the role of the countries of the region in helping the US to attack Iran have been documented,” Baghaei said at a news conference on Sunday, adding that Tehran was taking diplomatic action and would “follow up on this issue seriously”.

He said missiles, drones and aircraft launched from military bases in neighbouring countries as well as logistical support provided to US forces were proof of these nations’ involvement.

“The responsibility of this group of countries in the region for the consequences … of the military aggression of the United States and the Zionist regime against Iran is clear,” Baghaei charged, referring to Israel.

Attacks on its neighbours, he said, were justified under Article 51 of the United Nations Charter , which established the rights of states to defend themselves from attacks.

“No action has been taken by Iran against the sovereignty of these countries,” Baghaei said, arguing that Tehran’s attacks are “purely defensive in nature” and have targeted only US military bases and assets used to attack Iran.

Meanwhile, Jordan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates said in a post on X that it “condemned Iran’s brutal attacks on the sister kingdom of Bahrain as a flagrant violation of its sovereignty, a threat to its security, stability and territorial integrity”.

Egypt’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the country “reiterates its categorical rejection” of attacks threatening the region’s stability.

“The security of Bahrain and the Gulf states is closely linked to Egyptian national security and is one of the pillars of Arab national security,” the statement added.

articles.body: The US Army has named Lieutenant Colonel Brandon Carroll Tyner as the officer arrested in Britain over suspected espionage links to Russia. Tyner, who was stationed at a Nato military headquarters, is accused of attempting to assist Russian intelligence by obtaining sensitive military information.According to Defense News, citing a US Army official, Tyner, 41, was arrested in the United Kingdom as part of an investigation led by London's Counter Terrorism Policing. The FBI and US Army Counterintelligence Command are also assisting with the investigation.The allegations against Tyner centre on suspected attempts to assist Russian intelligence and obtain or disclose protected information. He was arrested under Sections 1 and 3 of Britain's National Security Act 2023, which criminalise obtaining or disclosing protected information and assisting a foreign intelligence service.FBI director Kash Patel described the arrest as a serious national security concern."This important arrest involves allegations of espionage, which is of the utmost concern to the United States and our allies," Patel said.According to The Wall Street Journal, Tyner was caught in an undercover sting operation after unknowingly speaking with British officials. He reportedly believed he was communicating with potential Russian contacts.Tyner joined the US Army in January 2008 as a human resources officer, holding the military occupational specialty 42H. According to the US Army, his previous deployments included Afghanistan, Qatar and Iraq.According to ABC News, Tyner also served with the Army's 82nd Airborne Division at Fort Bragg between 2011 and 2013. He was assigned to Imjin Barracks in Gloucestershire, which houses Nato's allied rapid reaction corps headquarters, at the time of his arrest.The case has raised concerns over the security of sensitive information within Nato's military command structure. The Allied rapid reaction corps (ARRC) is a multinational headquarters responsible for planning and coordinating land-force operations during military crises. Its work involves military planning, operational coordination and the deployment of allied forces.Brig General Sean Stinchon, commanding general of US Army Counterintelligence Command, also warned about insider threats."The alleged conduct of a senior soldier, entrusted with sensitive information, is a sobering reminder that insider threats are real and persistent," Stinchon said.Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov denied any Russian involvement in the case, saying Moscow had nothing to do with Tyner's arrest.Meanwhile, British police have searched two locations in Gloucestershire as part of the investigation. articles.body:
Al Jazeera English is marking 20 years since its official launch on November 15, 2006, about 10 years after Al Jazeera Arabic was inaugurated.

Since then, the channel and its digital footprint have grown dramatically in terms of content and coverage, becoming one of the most influential outlets in the world with employees from 78 nationalities and 48 bureaus around the world.

Here are some of the most significant developments we have covered over the years:

The war went on for 22 days. Israel’s widespread aerial bombing campaign on densely populated areas of the Palestinian enclave, including homes, police stations, schools, United Nations buildings and hospitals, was followed by a ground assault.

About 1,400 Palestinians and 13 Israelis were killed in the war that led to a blockade being imposed on the Gaza Strip.

In the years that followed, attempts by activists to break that siege were met with a brutal response from Israel. The deadliest of those Israeli attacks was on the Mavi Marmara, a ship that was part of the Gaza Freedom Flotilla, a convoy carrying more than 700 activists and 10,000 tonnes of humanitarian aid. Israeli soldiers boarded the vessel early in the morning on May 31, 2010, firing at the civilian passengers. Ten Turkish nationals were killed, and the attack set off a major diplomatic spat between Israel and Turkiye.

The series of pro-democracy and antigovernment protests , some of which led to armed rebellions after authorities brutally cracked down on them, started in December 2010 in Tunisia.

They swept across the Middle East and North Africa in the early 2010s, leading to multiple revolutions and shifts in power in Tunisia and Egypt , and prolonged conflicts in Syria , Libya and Yemen.

Many other countries introduced national reforms in light of the public movements going on across the region.

The Taliban movement returned to power in Afghanistan in 2021 in line with an agreement between the armed group and the United States.

The administration of US President Donald Trump signed the deal with the Taliban in Doha, Qatar, in February 2020, which set a timeline for the complete withdrawal of US troops and allied armies from Afghanistan.

As US troops withdrew, the Taliban continued to take control of the country. In August 2021, Taliban fighters entered the capital, Kabul, unopposed after President Ashraf Ghani fled the country.

In February 2022, the Russian army launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in a move widely perceived as unprovoked.

The attack, dubbed the “special military operation” by Moscow, resulted in widespread condemnation from the international community and started a brutal war , which is still ongoing.

Large chunks of eastern Ukraine – as well as the Crimean Peninsula, officially annexed by Moscow in 2014 – remain under Russian control today, with clashes and intense mutual aerial attacks on each other’s territory ongoing.

Qatar hosted the football World Cup in 2022 , the first in the Middle East and Arab world. Due to summer heat in the Gulf, it was the first World Cup held in late autumn and winter.

Argentina won the championship, defeating France in the final .

Israel launched its genocide against Palestinians in Gaza on October 7, 2023, and it is ongoing even today despite a so-called “ceasefire” agreed in October 2025.

The inhumane war started after Hamas’s armed wing, the Qassam Brigades, and other Palestinian groups attacked southern Israel, killing 1,139 people and taking about 240 others captive.

Since then, the enclave has been almost destroyed, and more than 74,600 people have been killed, according to local authorities.

The US and Israel launched strikes against Iran this February and started a war that killed many high-ranking Iranian officials, including the country’s supreme leader at the time, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

Since then, the sides have exchanged attacks numerous times, with the US forces hitting Iranian territory and Tehran targeting what it says are US assets in the region.

The conflict led Iran to effectively block navigation through the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway for hydrocarbon deliveries from the Gulf to the rest of the world, by attacking vessels passing through it.

The US, in response, imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports aimed at crippling the country’s economy.

The process to reach a deal between the sides continues under the mediation of Qatar and Pakistan.

articles.title: A Missouri therapist counselled a woman and her husband, then became intimately involved with the woman during sessions; after a jury awarded more than $2.1 million, a November 10 appeals court voided $1 million in punitive damages
articles.summary: A Missouri Court of Appeals has upheld most of a jury’s decision against a licensed therapist who became sexually involved with a woman during her
articles.body: A Missouri Court of Appeals has upheld most of a jury’s decision against a licensed therapist who became sexually involved with a woman during her counseling sessions, but it has removed $1 million in punitive damages from the judgment. The case, Anita Karase v. Craig Politte, was decided on November 10, 2026, and centres on allegations that Craig Politte exploited the therapeutic relationship with Anita Karase, a woman he had initially counselled alongside her husband, as mentioned on Justia U.S Law's website.The appeals court affirmed the jury’s findings on medical negligence, battery, and a violation of the Missouri Merchandising Practices Act. It reversed only the negligence per se claim, which had carried the $1 million punitive award, because it found that Missouri’s counselor ethics regulations do not create a separate private cause of action for that type of claim.How the relationship beganAccording to the court record, Politte began counselling Karase’s husband in 2018 through his private practice, Life Counseling Centers. He later provided couples therapy to Karase and her husband, then began seeing Karase individually.The court found that Politte did not discuss the potential conflict created by simultaneously providing couples and individual counseling to the same couple. Karase also did not sign an informed consent form before beginning therapy. After several individual sessions, Karase told Politte she was attracted to him. Physical contact between them intensified during sessions and eventually led to sexual acts, including intercourse.What the court foundThe jury found in Karase’s favour on all four counts. It awarded her $1,135,120 in compensatory damages and $1 million in punitive damages, for a total judgment of more than $2.1 million, as per the record. The jury assigned 99 percent fault to Politte and 1 percent fault to Karase on the medical negligence claim. On the negligence per se claim, it assigned 100 percent fault to Politte.Karase’s expert witness, licensed psychologist Dr. Catherine Hassler, testified that Politte breached the standard of care by treating both Karase and her husband and by failing to refer Karase to another counselor when she disclosed feelings for him. The court record notes that Politte admitted his conduct fell below the standard of care and that the sexual acts were intentional and harmful.Why the punitive damages were removedThe appeals court’s decision to strike the $1 million punitive award came down to a legal distinction. The jury had found Politte liable for negligence per se, a claim based on the argument that he violated specific professional regulations.But the appeals court held that Missouri’s counselor ethics regulations do not create a private cause of action that can support a negligence per se claim. In other words, while the regulations may justify professional discipline, they do not automatically give a client the right to sue for damages under that particular legal theory.Because the punitive damages were tied to that count, the court reversed that portion of the judgment and remanded the case for further proceedings. The rest of the jury’s verdict, including the compensatory damages, was affirmed.The human costThe case is not only about legal technicalities. It involves a woman who sought therapy during a difficult period in her life and later said she felt exploited by the person she trusted to help her.Karase told the court that she sought therapy with three other providers after the relationship ended, paying between $125 and $250 per session. She said she will need long-term mental health care because of the harm she experienced.The court also noted that Karase and her husband were in divorce proceedings by the time the relationship came to light. Karase initially resisted identifying Politte to her husband, hoping to protect him, before eventually disclosing what had happened.What happens nextThe appeals court’s ruling narrows the financial outcome but does not erase the jury’s finding that Politte was responsible for the harm Karase suffered. The compensatory damages remain in place, and the case will return to the lower court for further proceedings on the reversed count.The decision also clarifies an important legal boundary in Missouri. Professional ethics rules can lead to license discipline, but they do not necessarily create an independent path for a negligence per se lawsuit unless the legislature has clearly intended that result.For patients, the case is a reminder that the therapeutic relationship carries a duty of care. For counselors, it underscores that crossing professional boundaries can have consequences that extend beyond licensing boards and into the civil courts.You use AI every day. articles.title: South Korea's top scorer in tax accountancy exam admits cheating
articles.summary: Han Won-seok, 34, confessed to using a hidden camera and AI to get a near-perfect mark on the significant test.
articles.body:
A candidate who came first in South Korea's certified tax accountancy exam has admitted cheating by using a miniature camera, mobile phone and AI tools.

Han Won-seok confessed in a video on the YouTube account of his lawyer, Lee Don-Ho, adding that he had confessed to the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency and offered details on how he cheated.

The 34-year-old scored 397.5 out of 400 points in the first round, getting just one of 160 questions wrong, which initially raised suspicions and sparked online speculation.

Standardised national tests play an outsized role in career trajectories for South Koreans, making their results - and efforts to unduly inflate those results - of great importance.

"I cheated in both the first and second rounds of the tax account exam by using electronic devices and generative AI," Han said in the video published on Sunday.

"I used a microcamera to photograph the test questions and sent them to an AI then checked my answers on my smartphone to commit the cheating."

When accusations he had cheated first began to surface, Han had denied any wrongdoing - but said he had changed his mind after thinking about the feelings of the candidate who had come second in the exam.

He went on to apologise to the other entrants who had passed the tests fairly.

"It seems that because of me, other successful candidates are being suspected," he suggested.

The Ministry of Employment and Labour and the Human Resources Development Service held an emergency meeting after Han admitted cheating.

The South Korean president's policy chief Ha Jun-kyung said new measures would be introduced to prevent cheating and warned "past crimes" would be "tracked down and apprehended to the very end".

Those found to have used AI to cheat in the tax accountancy exam will have their qualification revoked and will be banned from retaking the test for five years, the government said.

The scandal comes just days before the east Asian nation's annual college entrance exam, a crucial hurdle for students.

Han said he had only cheated to try and earn money and get a job that would make his parents proud of him again.

Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency told Korean news agency Yonhap on Sunday that it was looking into the case.

"We received a written confession through the test taker's lawyer this morning regarding cheating on the tax accountant exam," it confirmed in a statement.

It added that the case had now been assigned to investigators.

Because of the significance of the national exams, instances of cheating are not uncommon in South Korea, and cases involving the use of AI have become more prominent as the technology becomes more sophisticated.

Last month, two college applicants were reported to have used AI glasses to try and cheat their entrance exams at two Seoul universities.

Education ministry data also says there were four cases of cheating through AI glasses at middle and high schools in the past 12 months.

articles.title: From Sonia-Natwar row to Advani's Jinnah remarks: 5 political memoirs that stirred storm
articles.summary: \"I will write my own book and then you will come to know everything.\" Sonia Gandhi's response to former external affairs minister Natwar Singh's explosive
articles.body: "I will write my own book and then you will come to know everything."Sonia Gandhi's response to former external affairs minister Natwar Singh's explosive autobiography in 2014 was as much a promise as it was a rebuttal. Singh's book had stirred a political storm with its account of why she declined the prime minister's post after the Congress-led UPA won the 2004 general elections. More controversially, he claimed that Rahul Gandhi had strongly opposed his mother's elevation, fearing she could meet the same fate as her husband, Rajiv Gandhi, and mother-in-law, Indira Gandhi, both of whom were assassinated. Sonia, who had publicly attributed her decision to her "inner voice", was now promising to tell her side of the story.Twelve years later, that promise has come full circle. Sonia Gandhi's memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, was released on November 10, bringing her own account of her life, family and political journey into the public domain. The book has already triggered political reactions and renewed debate over some of the most contentious episodes involving the Gandhi family.But Sonia is hardly the first political figure to find that putting personal recollections on paper can have consequences far beyond the pages of a book. Over the years, memoirs by politicians have revisited ideological battles, exposed differences within parties, offered personal accounts of political turning points and reopened controversies that many thought had been settled.From L K Advani's account of the Jinnah controversy to Jayaprakash Narayan's prison diary during the Emergency, these books have offered glimpses into the people and decisions behind some of India's defining political moments.Here are five political memoirs that made headlines for what their authors chose to reveal.Natwar Singh's One Life Is Not EnoughWhen Natwar Singh's autobiography was released in 2014, much of the attention centred on his account of Sonia Gandhi's decision not to become prime minister in 2004.While Sonia had publicly described the decision as a call of her "inner voice", Singh offered a different explanation. He claimed that Rahul Gandhi had strongly opposed his mother's elevation, fearing that she could meet the same fate as her husband, Rajiv Gandhi, and mother-in-law, Indira Gandhi, both of whom were assassinated.Singh wrote that Rahul's opposition was so strong that he gave Sonia 24 hours to decide. He also claimed that he, Manmohan Singh, Suman Dubey and Priyanka Gandhi were present when Sonia struggled with the decision. According to him, Rahul's intervention ultimately led her to offer the post to Manmohan Singh.The memoir went beyond the 2004 episode. Singh offered a sharply critical assessment of Sonia's leadership and her control over the Congress, describing her as increasingly authoritarian and secretive. He also recounted conversations with former prime minister P V Narasimha Rao, who, according to Singh, was troubled by Sonia's attitude towards him.The revelations triggered a political storm. Sonia rejected Singh's account and announced that she would write her own book. Former prime minister Manmohan Singh dismissed the claims as a "marketing gimmick", while the Congress accused Natwar Singh of distorting facts to promote his book.The controversy deepened when Singh made remarks linking Sonia's alleged ruthlessness to her Italian origin, drawing further criticism.LK Advani's My Country, My LifeReleased in New Delhi on March 19, 2008, by then President A P J Abdul Kalam, L K Advani's autobiography traced his journey from childhood in Karachi and Partition to his association with the RSS, the growth of the BJP, the Ram Janmabhoomi movement and his years in the Union government.One of its most discussed sections revisited the controversy surrounding Advani's June 2005 visit to Pakistan and his remarks on Muhammad Ali Jinnah. During the visit, Advani praised Jinnah's August 11, 1947, address to Pakistan's Constituent Assembly, in which the latter spoke about religious freedom and equal citizenship irrespective of religion.The remarks triggered a backlash within the BJP and the Sangh Parivar. Sections of the party viewed them as a departure from its ideological position, and Advani eventually resigned as BJP president.Looking back at the episode, Advani described it as "simply the most agonising moment of my political life". He also recalled feeling let down by several party colleagues during the controversy, contrasting their response with the support he had received during the Hawala case in 1996.Explaining the purpose of his Pakistan visit, he wrote: "I went to Pakistan as a messenger of peace, with an earnest desire to contribute to the normalisation of relations between our two long-estranged nations."Advani maintained that he had not described Jinnah as secular but had referred to a particular speech as a "classic, a forceful espousal of a Secular State". He also argued that the media had reported his remarks without adequately explaining their historical context.The autobiography also revisited the 1990 Rath Yatra and the demolition of the Babri Masjid on December 6, 1992. Another section offered insights into his long association with former prime minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.While acknowledging that the two sometimes differed in their approaches, Advani wrote that he had always regarded Vajpayee as his leader and generally deferred to his opinion.Mamata Banerjee's My Unforgettable MemoriesPublished in January 2012 by Roli Books, Mamata Banerjee's My Unforgettable Memories offered a personal account of the relationships, disappointments and political rivalries that shaped her career. The English book was a translation of excerpts from her earlier Bengali writings.It appeared just months after Mamata led the Trinamool Congress to a historic victory in the 2011 West Bengal assembly elections, ending the Left Front's 34-year rule. Her observations about prominent political figures, particularly Sonia Gandhi and Rajiv Gandhi, attracted considerable attention.Having spent years in the Congress before leaving the party to establish the Trinamool Congress in 1998, Mamata wrote about feeling repeatedly let down by its leadership. She referred to Sonia Gandhi as the "Queen Mother" and criticised the party's treatment of regional leaders."The culture in Congress is that when a regional faction gets too active, it's immediately censored by the top leadership," she wrote.Her account of Sonia, however, stood in contrast to the affection she expressed for Rajiv Gandhi, whom she described as "the leader of our hearts".Mamata recalled that after she was attacked at a rally in Kolkata in 1991 by alleged CPM activists, Rajiv took responsibility for arranging and paying for her treatment. He also sent people to ask whether she wanted to travel to the US for further medical care.She wrote that she was devastated when she heard of Rajiv's assassination in May 1991. She said she could neither eat nor speak to anyone for a week and described the loss as being "orphaned all over again, for the second time in my life since my father's death".The memoir also spoke warmly of former President Pranab Mukherjee, despite the changing political equations between the Congress and the Trinamool Congress."I have always respected him and my relationship with him is that of an elder brother and his kid sister," she wrote.She recalled that when Mukherjee was sidelined by the Congress and formed the Rashtriya Samajwadi Congress in 1986, she had repeatedly requested Rajiv Gandhi to take him back into the party.Jayaprakash Narayan's Prison DiaryUnlike the other books, Jayaprakash Narayan's Prison Diary was not a retrospective account written years after the events. It was a record of his experiences during one of the most turbulent periods in India's democratic history: the Emergency.Popularly known as JP, Narayan was among the most prominent leaders of the movement against Indira Gandhi's government in the 1970s. His call for Sampoorna Kranti (Total Revolution) had brought together students, opposition parties and civil society groups.After the Allahabad high court set aside Indira Gandhi's election from Rae Bareli on June 12, 1975, the movement gathered momentum. On June 25, JP addressed a massive rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan, calling for a peaceful struggle against the government. Hours later, the Emergency was proclaimed. In the early hours of June 26, opposition leaders, including JP, were arrested.Written during his detention and published by Popular Prakashan in 1977, the diary documented his experiences in custody, his health, his reading and his reflections on the political crisis.One of its most striking passages appeared in the opening entry, dated July 21, 1975, nearly a month after his arrest. JP wrote, "My world lies in a shambles all round me."He went on to express disbelief that a democratically elected prime minister could use the law to undermine democracy and suppress political opposition. The diary also contained sharp criticism of the decision to impose the Emergency, arrest opposition leaders and curtail civil liberties.Another deeply personal aspect of the book was its account of JP's deteriorating health. He was 72 when arrested and was already facing health problems. During his detention, his kidneys failed. He was released on November 12, 1975, on medical grounds and subsequently required regular dialysis for the remaining years of his life.Published in the year the Emergency ended and the Janata Party came to power, Prison Diary offered a contemporary first-person account of the political crisis from one of its most prominent opponents.Pranab Mukherjee's The Presidential YearsFormer President Pranab Mukherjee's The Presidential Years (2012-2017) made headlines even before its release in December 2020. The book offered his assessment of the Congress's decline, his dealings with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and some of the most consequential decisions taken during his presidency.Looking back at the Congress's defeat in the 2014 Lok Sabha elections, when the party won just 44 seats, Mukherjee attributed its performance to several factors, including its failure to recognise the end of its charismatic leadership. He described the establishment as having been reduced to a "government of averages".His observations also touched upon the Congress's leadership under Sonia Gandhi and Manmohan Singh.The memoir was equally candid about his interactions with Modi during his five-year tenure as President. Mukherjee described their relationship as cordial and said he had regularly offered the prime minister advice on policy matters. However, he criticised the NDA government's handling of Parliament between 2014 and 2019, blaming its "arrogance and inept handling" for the acrimonious exchanges between the treasury and opposition benches, while holding the opposition responsible too.One of the most discussed revelations concerned demonetisation. Mukherjee disclosed that Modi had not consulted him before announcing the decision on November 8, 2016. He said the lack of prior consultation did not surprise him, as the element of surprise was essential to such an announcement.He recalled that Modi visited Rashtrapati Bhavan after announcing the decision and explained its rationale. Mukherjee described demonetisation as a bold step but warned that it could cause a temporary economic slowdown and that the government would have to be careful about easing the burden on the poor.The memoir also became the subject of a family disagreement. Mukherjee's son, former Congress MP Abhijit Mukherjee, asked the publisher to halt publication until he had reviewed the final manuscript and given written consent. His daughter Sharmistha Mukherjee opposed the demand, saying their father had completed the manuscript before falling ill and that the final draft retained his handwritten notes and comments.Accusing her brother of creating "unnecessary hurdles", Sharmistha said preventing the book's release would be the "greatest disservice" to their departed father. The disagreement played out on social media, adding a family feud to the political conversations surrounding the memoir.Political memoirs offer a rare window into the personal experiences and perspectives of those who have occupied positions of power. They can reveal ideological differences, internal party dynamics and relationships that rarely find space in official accounts.But they are also personal interpretations of history. The authors decide which episodes to revisit, which conversations to disclose and how to explain decisions made years earlier. And, as the controversies surrounding these books show, sometimes what a politician writes long after leaving office can reopen debates that their public life had never quite settled.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Iran targets US military base in Bahrain with drone attack
articles.summary: It marks the second attack on the country in three days and comes as the US and Iran remain locked in a stand-off over the Strait of Hormuz.
articles.body:
Iran launched a drone attack against a US military base in Bahrain on Sunday, its second attempt to target the country in three days.

The country's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said it targeted the US air defence radar facility at al-Riffa air base in Bahrain using six drones.

Bahrain's military said its air defence systems intercepted and destroyed the Iranian air attacks "before they could achieve their objectives".

It comes after Iran fired drones at Bahrain on Friday, its first attack against Gulf countries since September.

The US and Iran are locked in a stand-off over the Strait of Hormuz. About a fifth of the world's gas and oil supply usually flows through it but shipping has been restricted since the outbreak of war in February.

Iran insists that it should control the strait and has been attacking what it calls "unauthorised" traffic, while the US military is providing protection for tankers shuttling oil through the strait to keep exports flowing from Gulf Arab states.

As sirens sounded across Bahrain on Sunday the interior ministry called on citizens to head to their nearest safe location.

Bahrain's foreign ministry said: "The Kingdom of Bahrain condemns in the strongest terms the continued brutal Iranian attacks on its territory and holds Iran fully responsible for their consequences."

In a statement on the strikes shared by Iran's state broadcaster on Telegram, the IRGC said: "The Strait of Hormuz is closed, and any aggression by the American enemy will be met with an even harsher and more forceful response."

Earlier this week, the IRGC claimed that it struck a US early warning radar system in Bahrain on Friday.

The US military has denied the claim, stating that the IRGC launched two one-way attack drones towards Bahrain and both were shot down by US forces. It added that there were no injuries or damage.

Earlier in the week the US carried out strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, US officials told CBS, the BBC's US partner.

The officials described the strikes as limited and defensive, and said they were in response to the IRGC firing on a US aircraft.

Iranian state news agency Irna reported explosions on Qeshm on Monday. The IRGC did not comment but said its forces had shot down two US MQM-170 drones south of the island and a US MQ-9 drone east of the Strait.

The US and Iran reached a preliminary agreement to end the war and reopen the strait in June, but it collapsed within weeks after Iranian attacks on shipping resumed and the US reinstated a naval blockade of Iranian ports.

Iranian negotiators had been discussing with mediators a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if the US meets seven conditions, reportedly including the lifting of the naval blockade and releasing frozen Iranian assets.

However this week Donald Trump said that the US was no longer interested in a deal to end the war with Iran and ordered Vice-President JD Vance, who had been involved in efforts to restart negotiations, to focus on domestic US politics.

articles.title: Can Netanyahu and Eisenkot form a ‘unity’ government in Israel?
articles.summary: Yashar and Likud are scheduled to hold talks on Sunday, but will need to overcome major differences to work together.
articles.body:
Israel’s caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has renewed his appeal for a unity government with opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, casting a coalition that would keep him in power as integral to Israel’s national security.

In a video statement on Saturday, Netanyahu said his meeting with Eisenkot on Thursday “only strengthened the conviction that it is essential to form a national unity government”. He said such a government could “eliminate the Iranian threat once and for all” and claimed Tehran would “not hesitate to use nuclear weapons against us”.

Eisenkot, the leader of the Yashar party and the man given the first shot to form Israel’s next government by President Isaac Herzog, called Netanyahu’s appeal a “bluff”.

“Nice try, but these tricks don’t work on me. Nor on Israel’s citizens,” Eisenkot said.

But Eisenkot confirmed that Yashar and Netanyahu’s Likud Party were talking about the proposal for a shared government.

So what, if anything, would it take for them to govern together, and what other options does Eisenkot have?

How do the numbers in the Knesset add up?

In Israel’s October 27 election, the four-party bloc led by Eisenkot won 48 of the 120 seats in the Knesset, Israel’s parliament. Netanyahu’s right-wing and religious bloc secured 53. Two Palestinian-led factions, the Joint List and Ra’am, also known as the United Arab List, won a record 19 seats between them.

Last week, Eisenkot’s bloc showed what it could do with the backing of both Palestinian-led factions, securing a 63-to-50 vote to approve the makeup of the Arrangements Committee, a panel that helps set the Knesset’s agenda while coalition talks are under way. The bloc then moved to set up temporary committees overseeing finance, foreign affairs and defence.

Eisenkot’s bloc and the two Arab-led factions hold 67 seats combined, six more than needed for an outright majority. Another possibility is a minority government backed by Ra’am’s eight lawmakers. Their support would give Eisenkot 56 votes against Netanyahu’s 53 if the Joint List’s 11 lawmakers abstained or stayed away from the confidence vote. That would allow a government to take office with fewer than 61 votes in favour, but it would depend on how all three groups voted.

But getting Eisenkot’s allies to agree to such a deal is another matter. Yair Golan, who leads the Democrats, is open to working with the Palestinian-led factions, while Yisrael Beiteinu leader Avigdor Lieberman and Together leader Naftali Bennett have rejected a coalition with Palestinians. However, both served in the government formed in 2021, when Ra’am became the first Arab party to formally join an Israeli governing coalition.

“One of Eisenkot’s main difficulties is the opposition of Avigdor Lieberman and Naftali Bennett [leaders of parties in his alliance] to relying on Arab parties,” Yasser Manna, a researcher at the Jerusalem Center for Studies on Israeli Affairs, told Al Jazeera. “This position restricts Eisenkot’s coalition options, but it does not automatically make a unity government with Netanyahu more likely. Instead, it increases the importance of negotiations with other parties, particularly the ultra-Orthodox parties.”

The other main option, which according to experts is the most likely scenario, is the Eisenkot bloc going into a coalition with both ultra-Orthodox parties in Netanyahu’s bloc, Shas and United Torah Judaism, which would take the Eisenkot bloc to 61.

Advisers from one faction of United Torah Judaism have reportedly sought a written commitment from all 48 lawmakers in Eisenkot’s bloc to pass a law exempting Jewish religious seminary students from military service and to shield it from being struck down by the High Court. Eisenkot and Lieberman are reportedly opposed to this compromise.

Could Eisenkot and Netanyahu govern together?

President Herzog gave Eisenkot until December 6 to form a government. Herzog can grant an extension of up to 14 days, which would take the deadline to December 20.

Eisenkot has left the door open to members of Netanyahu’s Likud Party and to far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich’s Religious Zionist Party, provided they back a government led by Eisenkot and accept his programme.

“If members of Likud and the Religious Zionist Party truly believe this is a time for unity, as they told the president, I cannot conceive of any reason why they would not support a government under my leadership and the principles I have presented,” Eisenkot said at the ceremony where Herzog handed him the mandate.

Daniel Levy, a former Israeli peace negotiator and president of the US/Middle East Project, told Al Jazeera that agreeing to meet can serve both men politically. “The coalition formation period is about spin and distortion and trying to gain leverage,” he told Al Jazeera. “So you take a meeting to show that you were willing to talk, then say the other side made unreasonable demands.”

The two men know each other well. Eisenkot led Israel’s military from 2015 to 2019 and served as an observer in Netanyahu’s war cabinet during the first eight months of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza. He left the emergency government in June 2024.

“I believe the relationship between Benjamin Netanyahu and Gadi Eisenkot is marked by a deep crisis of trust that goes beyond political competition,” Manna said. “However, it is important to distinguish between their political disagreements and their relatively similar approaches to national security. Both prioritise military and security considerations, particularly regarding the Palestinians and Iran.”

An early test could come on Tuesday, when Eisenkot’s allies plan to replace Knesset Speaker Amir Ohana of Likud with Yashar lawmaker Matan Kahana. Eisenkot has challenged Netanyahu and Smotrich to back Kahana and allow the vote to go ahead as scheduled, saying their response would show how serious they are about cooperation.

But even if Eisenkot and Netanyahu agreed on a policy plan for government, they still have to decide who leads. “The question of who would serve as prime minister remains the central obstacle,” Manna said. “Eisenkot has so far rejected a rotation arrangement with Netanyahu.”

Could a security crisis change the talks?

Meanwhile, Netanyahu is still in office as caretaker prime minister while negotiations continue. That gives him an incentive to exploit divisions among Eisenkot’s potential partners and wait for his mandate to run out, experts say.

“At this stage, Netanyahu does not necessarily need to form a new coalition himself,” Manna said. “Preventing Eisenkot from forming one may be enough to preserve his position temporarily.”

Manna said Netanyahu could also use a security crisis to increase pressure for a national government. “A renewed large-scale confrontation could increase pressure for a national unity government or shift the priorities of coalition negotiations,” he said. “At the same time, it could generate new disagreements over military decision-making, the management of the conflict, and the authority of a caretaker government.”

If talks with the ultra-Orthodox parties fail, Levy said, Eisenkot could ask his allies to choose between accepting support from the Palestinian-led parties and leaving Netanyahu in office. He could also propose a short-lived government whose immediate purpose would be to replace Netanyahu and prepare for another election.

He added that in such a scenario, Eisenkot might tell his allies to “form a government for a few months, just to get Bibi [Netanyahu] out of power and prepare for new elections”.

This would prevent Netanyahu from using “his position as prime minister to create a crisis”.

articles.title: Loch Ness Monster sightings jump in 2026 as scientist drills into legendary mystery
articles.summary: Even though Loch Ness Monster sightings have more than doubled in 2026, a University of St Andrews researcher explains that the spike is "nothing special" in his view.
articles.body: The Loch Ness Monster is making waves again amid an uptick in reported sightings — but one researcher told Fox News Digital he still isn't convinced the legendary Scottish creature is real. Reported sightings of Nessie, as the creature is popularly known, have more than doubled in 2026, climbing to 15 from six in 2025, according to the Official Loch Ness Monster Sightings Register. The register contains eyewitness accounts from visitors and locals around Loch Ness, a freshwater lake in the Scottish Highlands, roughly 20 miles southwest of Inverness. 1,000-YEAR-OLD CHURCH MYSTERY CRACKED BY STUDENTS FROM KING CHARLES' ALMA MATER In March, an American man said he saw "the dark-greenish gray body of what appeared to be Nessie emerge from the water." The man wrote, according to the register, "Nessie hovered for about 5 seconds, then dipped back into the water. Her body emerged against the chop of the surf, but appeared clearly defined against the waves, leading me to believe it wasn't just the current." In July, a local sailor said he saw a "large oversized crocodile head above the water" while he was out on his yacht. "The head quickly disappeared before I could get a photo," the man said. "It took me a few minutes to process what I was seeing. We made it into Fort Augustus safely with no further sightings." 'SIGNIFICANT' EARLY CHRISTIAN CHURCH EMERGES BENEATH FORMER FISH MARKET IN ANCIENT CITY One visitor from Malta said he saw a creature in August that looked like a "very large eel" moving against the current. "He estimated that the size was at least 7 meters [about 23 feet] in length," the register stated. Though the increase in sightings may seem significant, one expert disagrees. Charles Paxton, a research fellow in statistical ecology at the University of St. Andrews in Scotland, told Fox News Digital there was "nothing special" about the jump in reported sightings from 2025 to 2026. ARCHAEOLOGISTS UNCOVER EERIE ANGLO-SAXON 'SAND BODIES' AT NUCLEAR POWER STATION SITE "The numbers fluctuate a lot year on year," he said. Paxton said the modern phenomenon of Loch Ness Monster sightings began in the 1930s, particularly between 1933 and 1934. The reported sightings quickly became a major draw for tourists, bringing crowds to the area. "In 1934, the local government slashed its tourist budget, because they felt it wasn't necessary to do any advertising for tourism whatsoever," he said. "And there were traffic jams around the loch." ARCHAEOLOGISTS FIND ARTIFACTS OLDER THAN STONEHENGE BENEATH BRITAIN'S HOUSES OF PARLIAMENT: 'INCREDIBLY RARE' That surge of interest fell off over the years, but was revived again in the 1960s when the Loch Ness Investigation Bureau began collecting data on Nessie sightings. "And then, since the '70s, numbers have generally sort of dwindled, but with fluctuations" from year to year, Paxton said. Paxton also clarified that the database used to track modern sightings is not an official record, despite its name. "In a real sense, there isn't an official database," he said. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ "There are people collecting reports of the Loch Ness Monster from a variety of sources," added Paxton. "But that website has become a central location for people to [share] their reports." "People have these exciting, strange experiences, and the question is, what caused them?" Paxton, who is currently researching how cultural influences may contribute to reported sightings, said statistics can help researchers better understand why people report unusual experiences. "And people have these exciting, strange experiences, and the question is, what caused them? And I think we can use statistics to kind of investigate patterns in what's going on." "I don't think that's the case at all," he said. He cited several possible explanations, including "people seeing animals in the loch, people seeing boat wakes, people seeing wind waves, floating vegetation." articles.title: 20 years of Al Jazeera English: Our story is still being written
articles.summary: As we celebrate our 20th anniversary, we remain committed to our values and the quality of our journalism.
articles.body:
Twenty years ago today, on November 15, 2006, Al Jazeera English began broadcasting with a belief that the world needed a different perspective on the news. A perspective that would bring underreported stories to international attention and give people everywhere a greater opportunity to be seen and heard.

As we celebrate our 20th anniversary, that belief remains as important as ever.

The world has changed enormously over the past two decades. We have witnessed wars, political upheavals, economic crises, technological revolutions and profound changes in how people consume information. Through it all, Al Jazeera English has sought to do more than report events. We have worked to explain why they matter, explore their impact on people’s lives and help audiences understand an increasingly complex world.

Our journey has never simply been about building another international news channel. It has been about broadening the global conversation.

From the beginning, Al Jazeera English sought to broaden international news coverage by bringing greater diversity of perspectives, voices and stories to audiences around the world.

We believed that events everywhere deserved attention, depth and serious journalism, regardless of where they took place. We also believed that people experiencing conflict, injustice, poverty and political change should not be merely subjects of news coverage, but voices within it.

This approach has helped define our editorial identity. It reflects our belief that no single perspective can fully explain our world, and that good journalism must question assumptions, examine different viewpoints and bring important stories to light.

At the heart of this philosophy is a simple principle: every human life matters, and every story deserves to be approached with dignity and fairness.

Behind every broadcast, investigation, documentary and breaking news story are people whose dedication makes our work possible.

Al Jazeera English brings together colleagues representing 78 nationalities, reflecting the diversity of cultures, experiences and perspectives that make our channel unique.

I think particularly of our journalists working in difficult and sometimes dangerous circumstances, often far from their families, determined to tell stories the world needs to hear.

I also think of the many colleagues working behind the scenes, whose contributions may not always be visible to audiences but remain essential to everything we achieve.

We must remember those who helped build this channel over the past two decades, including colleagues who are no longer with us. Their dedication and sacrifices are part of our history.

Our greatest achievement is not any single programme, interview or award. It is the collective effort of generations of people who have believed in the purpose of this channel.

The media landscape is changing at an extraordinary pace. Audiences have more choice than ever before, but also face an overwhelming volume of information, misinformation and competing narratives. Artificial intelligence is transforming how content is produced and distributed, while traditional viewing habits continue to evolve.

These developments present challenges, but also opportunities.

We must embrace innovation, explore new storytelling formats and meet audiences wherever they choose to engage with news. But technological progress must never come at the expense of what makes journalism valuable.

Technology cannot replace editorial judgement, human understanding, compassion or the responsibility to establish what is true.

Credibility is earned through consistent, rigorous journalism. Trust takes years to build and can be lost quickly. Neither should ever be taken for granted.

Today, as we celebrate our 20th anniversary, Al Jazeera English also unveils a new on-air look, marking the beginning of another chapter in our journey. But our ambitions extend well beyond what audiences see on their screens.

We want to strengthen our journalism, deepen our storytelling, develop fresh ideas and engage meaningfully with audiences around the world.

Equally important is building a workplace culture based on respect, trust, fairness, openness, collaboration and accountability. A place where people feel valued, ideas are welcomed and everyone has an opportunity to contribute and grow.

Great journalism requires talented people. Sustaining it requires an environment where they can do their best work.

Twenty years is a significant milestone, but not a destination.

We should be proud of what Al Jazeera English has achieved, while recognising that our continued relevance must be earned every day through the quality of our journalism, the strength of our values and our willingness to evolve.

The world still needs journalism that questions power, challenges assumptions, brings neglected stories to light and places humanity at the centre of its reporting.

That was our promise in 2006. Twenty years later, it remains our responsibility.

Our first 20 years have shaped who we are. What we do next will define who we become.

The views expressed in this article are the author’s own and do not necessarily reflect Al Jazeera’s editorial stance.

articles.title: Lions star’s knee buckles celebrating sack of Patriots’ Drake Maye as both injured on same play
articles.summary: Aidan Hutchinson injured his right knee during a sack celebration at Munich's Allianz Arena on the same play that Drake Maye hurt his ankle.
articles.body: The first quarter of the NFL game in Munich's Allianz Arena has been an injury disaster. Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson injured his right knee and New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye suffered an ankle injury. Both are out of the game, although only the Patriots have made that status official for Maye. The Lions officially have kept Hutchinson's status as questionable to return even though he has not returned to the game. Both were apparently injured on the same play when Hutchinson sacked Maye. DRAKE MAYE TELLS REPORTERS THEY DON'T KNOW 'WHAT THEY'RE TALKING ABOUT' DURING GERMANY PRESS CONFERENCE Maye left the field, limping slowly back to the Patriots' locker room, and is questionable to return. He was replaced in the lineup by Tommy DeVito. The Patriots officially ruled Maye out of the game in the second quarter. Hutchinson injured himself in the most unorthodox and unfortunate manner after his sack of Maye – during his sack celebration. The former Michgan standout sacked Maye on a key third down passing situation. He arose and immediately separated to celebrate. That celebration involved Hutchinson leaping into the air with his clenched right fist raised in celebration. And when Hutchinson hit the ground, his right knee buckled and the Lions defensive end crumpled to the field at Allianz Arena. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Hutchinson grabbed his right knee as he lay on the field in obvious pain. He was eventually taken into the Lions' medical tent and then walked into the team's locker room. The Lions said Hutchinson is questionable to return to the game. Hutchinson has five sacks this season. He missed all but five games in 2024 when he suffered a broken tibia and fibula on his left leg.

articles.title: Supertanker with 2 million barrels of oil sinks after hitting mine in Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary: A supertanker carrying more than two million barrels of crude oil has sunk after striking a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Islamic
articles.body: A supertanker carrying more than two million barrels of crude oil has sunk after striking a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said on Sunday.The IRGC have claimed that two oil tankers had hit mines while attempting to cross an unauthorised route in the southern part of the strait, triggering explosions and fires. The supertanker carrying two million barrels of crude oil was one amongst the two tankers reported. The claim could not be independently verified, and the Guards did not identify either vessel or disclose their country of origin.The announcement came as the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) centre reported a separate tanker attack in the Gulf, based on information received from Indian shipping authorities. It said the crew were safe, but the extent of damage and any environmental impact remained unknown. It was not clear whether this was one of the incidents cited by Iran.Iran warns ships against unauthorised routesIn a statement carried by Iranian state television, the IRGC said the two tankers had struck naval mines after entering a prohibited route. It claimed the vessels had switched off their identification and positioning systems to pass through the area covertly, and alleged they had US military support.The Guards said one of the vessels, a supertanker carrying more than two million barrels of crude, sank in the southern waters of the Persian Gulf. It did not provide further details about the second tanker.Iran's state-run IRNA news agency separately reported that five oil tankers had struck mines and caught fire in the waterway over the preceding 48 hours. The agency said two incidents occurred near Oman's coast, while three others were reported in the central and eastern sections of the strait.Hormuz remains a flashpointSince the outbreak of the Middle East war in late February, Tehran has sharply restricted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, insisting that vessels use routes authorised by Iran. It has repeatedly reported attacks on ships it says attempted to transit without permission.The United States has responded with a naval blockade of Iranian ports and support for tankers seeking to cross the waterway. US Central Command said last month that it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil through the strait since the summer.The US military had also recently said it had cleared all mines from the main shipping routes through Hormuz.You use AI every day. articles.title: Chris Van Hollen hits back at Sean Duffy over Congress funding criticism after US ground stop
articles.summary: Senator Chris Van Hollen responds to Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy's blame on Congress for a funding shortfall linked to a recent nationwide ground stop, emphasizing the approved funding from the Trump administration.
articles.body: Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen has slammed Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy for blaming Congress over the funding shortfall he said contributed to Friday’s nationwide ground stop, arguing that lawmakers had already approved the money requested by the Trump administration.Speaking to CNN’s Dana Bash on State of the Union, Van Hollen said Duffy’s response to the disruption was to shift responsibility to Congress, despite the administration having received billions of dollars through legislation passed by Republicans.“Unfortunately Secretary Duffy’s first response just the other day was to point fingers and blame Congress,” Van Hollen said. He added that Congress had met the administration’s funding request and that Republicans had included $12.5 billion for the department in their so-called “Big Beautiful Bill”.Van Hollen also questioned how much of that allocation had been used, saying the administration had spent only about one-third of the money.“So it’s really rich to hear the secretary pointing the fingers at Congress when Congress has given the administration what they asked for,” he told Bash.The Maryland senator said he would support additional funding if it was necessary, but insisted that administration officials should explain their requirements to lawmakers before receiving more money. He called on them to come to Congress and justify the additional request.Duffy, meanwhile, has urged Congress to provide his department with another $50 billion, arguing that the money was needed to support infrastructure development. He called on lawmakers to set aside political differences and scrutinise how the funds would be spent.“Let’s put away the partisanship. Just do oversight on me. Ask how I’m going to spend the money. Make sure I spend the money well. But give me the resources to actually build on behalf of the American people,” Duffy said.The exchange followed Friday’s nationwide ground stop and the travel disruption that came after it. Duffy said President Donald Trump had been closely involved in the administration’s response, despite not publicly addressing the incident on social media until Sunday.You use AI every day.
