articles.title: Clothing factories shut in Bangladesh as workers strike over pay
articles.summary: Workers are striking over demands for a minimum wage of 30,000 taka (£182) a month.
articles.body:
Dozens of factories in Bangladesh's main clothes-producing area have been shut by workers striking over a higher minimum wage.

Nearly 150 sites across the country have been closed in the textile hubs of Savar, Ashulia and Gazipur this weekend.

The garment industry is big business for Bangladesh, generating nearly $40bn (£30bn) in exports every year and making up 10% of the country's total GDP.

Workers are striking over demands for a minimum wage of 30,000 taka (£182) a month. The minimum monthly wage in Bangladesh is currently 12,500 taka but employees say this is not enough to deal with the cost of living crisis.

On Sunday morning workers massed on the Dhaka-Tangail highway in Gazipur to block the road. Traffic was stopped by the protests for about an hour before police stepped in.

A "No Work No Pay" provision of labour laws allows owners to suspend operations and withhold wages when production is disrupted.

Police Supt Mohammad Amjad Hossain told the BBC officers shut factories in the city after the workers walked out.

He said 13 factories were closed on Saturday night and "sixteen factories were closed during the morning unrest".

Wage protests force hundreds of Bangladesh garment factories to close

The garment industry in Bangladesh employs about four million workers making clothes for big brands including H&M, Primark and Zara.

Bangladesh is the world's second largest exporter of ready- to-wear clothes after China and it is feared that the current unrest could have a knock-on effect for international buyers if it carries on for substantial amount of time.

The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) and the Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BKMEA) is calling for protection for factories.

"BGMEA and BKMEA have questioned the justification of continuing to participate in wage board negotiations without any assurance that the factories will be protected," BGMEA President Mahmud Hasan Khan said.

"Garment factories that have been unable to continue production due to the ongoing unrest will remain indefinitely closed from tomorrow under... Bangladesh's labour law."

On 1 November the government formed a minimum wage board to recommend a revised pay structure for workers.

The board, chaired by a senior district judge, said at its first meeting it would finalise any recommendations by the end of November.

Once it is put in place, the revised pay structure is expected to take effect from 1 December.

articles.summary: 19-year-old BCom student Bhavishya Sharma died after a truck hit his bike on Tumakuru Road; friend injured. Separate Bengaluru crash hurt a 9-year-old girl.
articles.body: Bengaluru: A 19-year-old BCom student was killed and his friend injured after a truck rammed their motorcycle and ran over him while they were heading for a trekking trip to Shivagange Hills in the early hours of Sunday.The deceased has been identified as Bhavishya Sharma, a second-year BCom student at a private university on Hosur Main Road. He was a native of Haryana, and his parents have settled in Dubai. He was staying in a hostel for his studies. His friend Anushka (19), who was riding pillion, sustained injuries and is undergoing treatment at a hospital. The BSc student was out of danger, police said, quoting the doctors.Based on a preliminary investigation, police said eight students travelling on four motorcycles had set out from Koramangala for Shivagange Hills near Dobbaspete. Around 2.30 am, when they reached Parle-G Gate on Tumakuru Road, a truck allegedly rammed the motorcycle ridden by Bhavishya.The impact caused the motorcycle to lose balance, throwing both riders off. Bhavishya fell towards the right side and was run over by the truck, killing him on the spot. Anushka fell towards the left.Peenya traffic police detained the truck driver, Ramanath Tivari. He was not found to be under the influence of alcohol. Further investigation is on.Girl hurt in accidentA nine-year-old girl suffered serious head injuries after a bike hit her while she was crossing the road at Hesaraghatta, north Bengaluru, Friday morning. The incident was captured on CCTV cameras.Madhumitha, a class 4 student, was returning home after buying milk when the bike hit her, throwing her into the air. articles.title: Duffy says Trump was ‘fully engaged’ during US flight disruptions despite delayed public response
articles.summary: US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy defends President Trump's involvement in handling the nationwide flight disruptions, emphasizing his leadership despite a delayed public response.
articles.body: US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy has said President Donald Trump remained closely involved in the government's response to the nationwide flight ground stop on Friday, despite not publicly addressing the disruption until Sunday.Speaking on CNN's State of the Union with Dana Bash, Duffy said Trump's involvement had been significant throughout the aviation crisis. His remarks came after the president faced questions over his silence on social media while thousands of passengers dealt with flight delays and cancellations.Asked about Trump's lack of public comments on the disruption, Duffy said the president's engagement had been "remarkable"."His insight into how we have to come together as Americans ... to get this done is, I think, a sign of great leadership," Duffy told Bash.He added that Trump had been monitoring developments throughout the incident."The president is fully supportive, fully engaged, and was fully tracking what's happening," Duffy said.Duffy also said Trump had offered to make resources from other government departments available to address the aviation system's problems.
